lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet has a way of exposing the blueprint. Toronto's most consequential offseason move so far is off the ice - the hire of Andy O'Brien to run sport performance - a sign the Leafs are trying to squeeze more out of the same core without pretending this was a one-fix summer. The club also added Jack Roslovic in free agency, and he already calls Toronto the right fit, while the prospect board is getting its own polish with Landon Sim at No. 19 and Nick Moldenhauer at No. 20. That is the shape of August: no drama, just calibration. There is no scoreboard to hide behind, and the final record only underlines how much the next camp matters. Watch for the September health check, the fourth-line race, and whether the new performance staff can sharpen the edges before training camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The trade deadline left Toronto with a roster that looks remade on the fly - and the newest jolt is Trey Yesavage leaving early and heading for an MRI on his knee, a reminder that even the fresh blood comes with risk. The Blue Jays sit in the offseason after finishing 2026 at 97-65, and the front office has spent the last week trying to steady a rotation that suddenly feels in flux again. Deadline arrivals gave the club volume, but volume is not the same as certainty. Yesavage is the name fans will track first, because a healthy young arm can change the winter's mood; an injured one only sharpens the pressure on the next wave of pitching depth. What matters now is whether Toronto can turn deadline chaos into a coherent winter plan before camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet has settled over the Raptors' summer, but it's the useful kind - the kind that lets a front office finish the broom work and map out camp. Toronto used its final two-way slot on centre Trey Jemison, a plain-dealing move that deepens the frontcourt behind Jakob Poeltl and Trayce Jackson-Davis and gives the club a sturdy body for the grind ahead. The Raptors are still in the deep offseason, with no games to chase and no scoreboard to flatter them, so the real story is roster construction: one more big, one less hole. Jemison's arrival gives the organization a cleaner look at the 21-man offseason group and a little more competition for the 15-man cutdown. What matters next is training camp - and whether Jemison can turn a two-way into a real seat at the table.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The roster is still taking shape, and training camp is already separating the useful from the ornamental. Ahkello Witherspoon's retirement opened a fresh cornerback hole, and Washington answered by signing Fabian Moreau - a clean, practical move in a camp built on competition. Jayden Daniels' name keeps rising, too; league chatter has him in the 13th-overall quarterback tier, while the real camp story is his growing command of the offense and the receivers fighting to be trusted. Treylon Burks has flashed with the first unit, Jaden Bradley is pressing for a 53-man argument, and the depth chart at wideout is anything but settled. With Washington in the thick of camp and the preseason looming, watch the padded practices - those are where the final roster edges get carved.
